The Constraints That the Kinks Place on the Stacked Coefficients

Source: R/outer_refresh.R
kink_constraints.Rd

Reads, through modelterms7::term_kink_constraints(), the linear constraints that hold the objective on its kinks at the coefficients given, for every term that recomputes its own block, and places their rows in the columns of the stacked vector.

Usage

kink_constraints(spec, design, coef, split, total)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

design

The design.

coef

The coefficients, a named list with one numeric vector per parameter.

split

The stacked positions of each parameter's coefficients, a named list as the objective's split returns it for seq_along() of the stacked vector.

total

The length of the stacked vector.

Value

A numeric matrix with total columns and one row per constraint, with no rows if the design has no term with a kink.

Details

A break-point that sits on an observation is a kink of the objective. Where its position is a single coefficient the row is that coefficient's unit vector; where the position is developed over a design the row is the development's row of that observation, and the coefficients can still move along the hyperplane on which the break-point stays on the observation. iwls_fit() solves on that subspace where a line search rejects every step length, and mode_solver() moves the mode in it.

See also

iwls_fit(), mode_solver(), refresh_units().
